title: Sanofi Invests in Insulin Plant in Frankfurt
content:
Sanofi Invests in Insulin Plant in Frankfurt
Prioritise Us
on Google
Rendering of the new insulin manufacturing facility at Sanofi BioCampus Frankfurt. Credit: Sanofi
Sanofi CEO Belén Garijo outlines how a multi-billion Frankfurt facility will use AI and automation to strengthen Europe’s insulin supply
Sanofi has begun construction of a nearly EUR2bn (US$2.24bn) insulin manufacturing facility at its Frankfurt BioCampus, securing a long-term European production base for human insulin.
Planned to enter full production in 2032, the 36,000-square-metre site will use modern automation, digital systems and
artificial intelligence
manufacturing
and quality operations, replacing an existing older insulin production facility on the same site.
“Millions of people around the world rely on insulin every day, and our commitment to them is for the long term. With this new facility, we are investing in the next generation of insulin manufacturing in Europe, building on more than a century of expertise and a strong industrial footprint in Frankfurt. Maintaining the right conditions for investment and innovation will be essential to Europe’s future competitiveness,” said Belén Garijo
Chief Executive Officer, Sanofi.
Belén Garijo, CEO of Sanofi. Credit: Sanofi.
Sanofi retains insulin manufacturing in Germany
The new facility will be built at Sanofi’s integrated Frankfurt BioCampus. The site covers the insulin value chain from active pharmaceutical ingredient production through filling, device assembly and packaging.
The new plant will occupy an area equivalent to approximately five football fields and is expected to become one of Europe’s largest and most advanced insulin manufacturing facilities once operational.
The new facility is intended to strengthen the company’s ability to maintain supply over the long term as global demand changes. Sanofi says more than 500 million people worldwide live with diabetes, while the number is expected to exceed 800 million by 2050.
The investment therefore has significance beyond Germany. The Frankfurt site will continue to form part of Sanofi’s global insulin supply network, and continue supplying about 80 countries with 20 insulin products.
Sanofi currently supplies insulin to approximately 15 million people in more than 100 countries each year, according to the company.
Without the investment, Sanofi had warned that production of human insulin at its Frankfurt-Höchst site would cease. About 6,500 people work at Sanofi’s Frankfurt site, including more than 4,000 in its insulin operations.
Representatives from Sanofi and regional German politics attended the opening ceremony at Sanofi's Frankfurt BioCampus. Credit: Belén Garijo via LinkedIn
Production planned for 2032
Construction began following the European Commission’s approval in September 2026 of EUR400m (US$448.82m) of public support from the German Federal Government, the State of Hesse and the City of Frankfurt under the European Union’s state-aid framework. Sanofi initially announced a project investment of approximately EUR1.3bn (US$1.46bn) in 2024. The company now describes the total investment in the Frankfurt facility as nearly EUR2bn (US$2.24bn).
The European Commission’s approval of state aid stipulates that the site produces at least 1.1 tonnes of insulin per year at the site through 2042, and retains a reserve of 1.0t of insulin active pharmaceutical ingredients through 2042.
The aid also requires that Sanofi prioritises sales to European Economic Area (EEA) markets in the event that shortages occur.
Frankfurt-Höchst is the only site producing human insulin in the European Economic Area and one of just two insulin production sites in the EU together with a Novartis production facility in Denmark.
Sanofi currently operates an insulin production facility on its Frankfurt campus. Credit: Sanofi
Key facts about the Sanofi's new production facility
Location: The plant is being built at Sanofi’s BioCampus in Frankfurt, Germany.
Footprint: The facility will cover approximately 36,000 square metres.
Production: Full production of insulin active pharmaceutical ingredients is planned for 2032, subject to licensing.
EU support: Germany received European Commission approval for EUR400m (US$448.82m) in state aid.
Annual output: Sanofi must produce at least 1.1 tonnes of insulin annually at the site.
Strategic reserve: The company must hold 1 tonne of insulin active pharmaceutical ingredients at the site through 2042.
Market priority: EEA markets must be prioritised during insulin shortages.
A boost for European pharma manufacturing
The development represents a large-scale investment by Sanofi in pharmaceutical manufacturing capacity in Europe after a sustained series of investments by European-headquartered groups such as AstraZeneca and Bayer in new or planned manufacturing facilities in the US.
The investment by Sanofi will ensure that Germany will remain an export hub for human insulin production and global supply chains until 2042.
Meet the Partners
1. Sanofi
: US$53.92bn
Employees
: 77,440
: Belén Garijo
Sanofi engages in the research, production, and distribution of pharmaceutical products. It operates through the Biopharma segment, which comprises commercial operations and research, development and production activities relating to the specialty care, general medicines and vaccines franchises plus support and corporate functions, for all geographical territories.
AstraZeneca
: US$215.94bn
Employees
: 42,000
: Pascal Soriot
AstraZeneca is a global biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialisation of prescription medicines. Its portfolio spans oncology, rare diseases, and biopharmaceuticals, including cardiovascular, renal & metabolism, and respiratory & immunology.

title: Amazon’s Holiday Expansion: New Jobs and Worker Stability
content:
Amazon’s Holiday Expansion: New Jobs and Worker Stability
Prioritise Us
on Google
Amazon is increasing its seasonal staff numbers. Credit: Amazon
Amazon is investing in its future workforce with its expanded holiday hiring and new company benefits, Udit Madan, SVP Worldwide Operations explains
Amazon has opened its seasonal job opportunities, with new benefits being introduced and a clear pathway to long-term employment at the company.
As holiday shopping continues to increase
demand for the ecommerce giant
, Amazon is hiring more people than in previous years.
Alongside that, it is investing in worker wellbeing – protecting employees and developing greater resilience for its future operations.
Logistics expansion
This holiday season, Amazon is hiring more than 300,000 people for
seasonal, part-time and full-time roles
across its US network. These jobs will be available across Amazon’s core operations across the nation, working across fulfilment centers, customer service, driver network, in-store and at locker locations.
As holiday shopping begins to increase, Amazon will be facing greater demand than any other time in the year. Customers will be buying decorations, presents and food and drink online. Already, the platform is releasing deals – its Holiday Beauty Event running from 19th October - 1st November. Events like these help customers shop in advance while saving money, and also ensures Amazon becomes the go-to place for gift purchasing.
With this comes the need for a broader staff base, meeting the rising demand of shoppers while also maintaining the Prime promise of affordable prices and speedy delivery.
“This holiday season, Amazon is hiring over 300,000 people across the US in our core operations — 20% higher than last year, and one of the largest seasonal hiring pushes in the country,” Udit Madan, Senior Vice President, Worldwide Operations at Amazon posts to LinkedIn.
Udit Madan, Senior Vice President, Worldwide Operations at Amazon
“For many, a season here can turn into something more. Every year, people who start with a seasonal job stay and build careers here, becoming trainers, managers and leaders across our network.”
Amazon’s seasonal hiring acts as an opportunity to gain new work experience and
For many, this represents a new opportunity to gain a solid introduction into Amazon’s operations, as Amazon
invests in its future workforce
At a glance
More than 300,000 people will be hired as part of Amazon’s holiday job postings
Seasonal employees working 30+ hours a week will have healthcare coverage from day 1, beginning on January 1, 2027
Seasonal employees will earn an average of US$20/hour
Amazon will be posting new job openings weekly
Many of the employees will stay on for long-term employment
Investments into the workforce
This year, Amazon is introducing increased benefits to its workforce, including more stability and increased pay. In doing so, it is strengthening its supply chain stability and demonstrating investments into the people within the company.
“The holidays are my favorite time of year at Amazon,” explains J. Ofori Agboka, Vice President - People, Experience and Technology at Amazon.
“There’s an energy across our operations network that’s hard to match as our teams come together to deliver for customers during our busiest season. One of the best parts is welcoming so many new teammates into Amazon and, this year, we’re hiring over 300,000 people for seasonal, part-time and full-time roles across our core operations network nationwide.
J. Ofori Agboka, Vice President - People, Experience and Technology at Amazon.
“As we welcome those new teammates, we’re also continuing to invest in the people who make all of this possible and the benefits that matter most to them and their families.”
For several years, Amazon has been offering healthcare support to its regular, full-time employees starting on day one of their contract.
Company benefits
The online retailer is investing in its staff in other ways. It has announced more than US$1.5bn in higher pay for its US core operations workforce. This breaks down to seasonal staff being paid an average of US$20 an hour. Full-time core operations employees now earn a minimum starting wage of US$20 an hour.
The company is also helping paychecks go further – Amazon employees across the US now get a 10% discount on eligible groceries and everyday essentials on Amazon.com and Whole Foods Market online, as well as a 20% discount in Whole Foods Market stores.
Seasonal jobs offer employees an opportunity to earn money,
learn new skills
and work flexible hours. For some, it is a temporary role, but for others it is their start on the Amazon ladder.
Many seasonal employees have become trainers, managers and leaders, nurtured in these roles through various upskilling programmes and training.
As we welcome those new teammates, we’re also continuing to invest in the people who make all of this possible and the benefits that matter most to them and their families.
J. Ofori Agboka, Vice President - People, Experience and Technology at Amazon
Key companies
Amazon is the world's largest e-commerce retailer, operating an extensive global logistics network of fulfillment centers, delivery stations, and last-mile infrastructure. Founded in 1994, the company employs over 1.5 million people worldwide. Amazon's operations include Prime delivery, Amazon Web Services, and Whole Foods Market. The company invests over $1.5bn annually in US workforce wages, maintaining competitive advantages through operational excellence.
Whole Foods
Acquired by Amazon in 2017 for $13.7bn, Whole Foods Market serves as both a retail subsidiary and integrated fulfillment hub within Amazon's omnichannel supply chain. The grocery chain offers Amazon employees exclusive benefits including 20% in-store discounts and 10% online discounts. Whole Foods locations function as pickup points, delivery hubs, and employment centers, bridging physical and digital retail operations during peak holiday demand.

The new EV will follow the EX60 as the second vehicle based on
SPA3 platform, positioned as a smaller, more affordable option.
Volvo enters lower-priced EV market in 2027
As part of Volvo’s largest product offensive, the company plans to launch 13 new cars through the end of 2030.
All new vehicles will be tailored to specific markets, including the US, Europe, and China. Volvo announced during its third-quarter earnings on Friday that it will reveal three of the new vehicles in 2027.
One of the new vehicles will be for Europe and the other two are destined for China (more on the US later).
Following the EX60, which Volvo said has been “a big success,” racking up
over 50,000 orders
in Europe so far, Volvo will launch the second electric car based on its SPA3 platform.
According to Volvo the new model is a “global BEV car, which targets a large, lower priced market segment” in Europe. The first customer deliveries are set to begin after next summer.
(Source: Volvo Cars Q3 2026 earnings presentation)
While the company didn’t reveal any further details, the new vehicle is suspected to be the successor to the current EX40.
The SPA3 platform supports everything from sedans and compact SUVs like the EX30 to the three-row EX90. As a mass-market vehicle, the new SPA3-based EV will likely be an SUV.
Will Volvo bring the lower-priced EV to the US? It said it was a “global BEV car,” but also that it was aimed at Europe’s lower-priced segment.
Volvo EX60 reveal event (Source: Volvo)
Luis Rezende, president of Volvo Cars America, told reporters during a media roundtable (via
TheVerge
) earlier this year that the company is preparing to launch a new EV in 2027 that will replace the EX30 as its new entry-level electric car.
Volvo initially said the lower-priced Single Motor EX30 would go on sale in the US in late 2025 starting at $34,950, but later backtracked and
discontinued the electric SUV
Volvo EX30 (Source: Volvo)
Although it may not be as cheap as the entry-level $35,000 EX30, Renzende said prices would be “very similar.”
According to an
Automotive News
report, Volvo will launch the new electric crossover SUV by the end of 2027, starting at under $50,000.
The new entry-level model is expected to go on sale as the EX50, a taller and longer electric SUV than the current EX40.
Volvo EX50 trademark filing (Source: EUIPO)
filed a trademark
with the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) for EX50 in July. Although the filing didn’t reveal many details, it did confirm it will be electric.
In the meantime, Volvo is fast-tracking production of its
first long-range plug-in hybrid
versions of the XC90 and XC60. The first customer deliveries are set to begin this year in Europe, followed by the US shortly after.
In Q1 2027, Volvo will begin production of the XC60 in Charleston. By the end of 2030, it plans to begin production of a “second, all-new car with multiple powertrain options,” the company said.

title: Volvo says the EX60 will be a best-seller with over 50,000 orders in Europe already
content:
Peter Johnson
| Oct 23 2026 - 7:53 am PT
expects the EX60 to become one of its best-selling vehicles ever, with over 50,000 orders already in Europe. But as demand builds, Volvo is struggling to ramp up production.
Volvo EX60 orders top 50,000 as production lags behind
After reporting third-quarter earnings on Friday, Volvo said the EX60 has been “a big success” so far, receiving over 50,000 orders in Europe since production began in April.
However, the company has built only around 5,000 units so far because of “new industrial technology,” Volvo said, such as the EX60’s cell-to-body structural battery design and manufacturing changes required for its new SPA3 platform.
The Swedish automaker admitted that the production ramp-up is “taking longer than planned,” but promised volumes are steadily improving.
Volvo Car’s president and CEO Håkan Samuelsson said the EX60 will be a cornerstone of Volvo’s comeback plan as one of its most profitable models, but warned that the financial impacts will not be realized until volume picks up.
After delivering the first models in Europe this summer, Volvo planned to ramp up production as the EX60 arrived in new markets, including the US.
Volvo EX60 orders reach over 50,000 in Europe (Source: Volvo Cars Q3 2026 earnings)
Volvo initially expected to sell about 7,000 EX60s in the US by the end of 2026, but a dealer told
Automotive News
last week that the company is on pace to deliver just a fraction of that.
In a note sent to dealers in late September, Volvo said it had
delayed customer deliveries
in the US. A company spokesperson confirmed that EX60 availability will “remain limited” in the short term. In early 2027, Volvo expects to distribute significantly more inventory to dealers.
The delay comes at a crucial point as Volvo aims to lower its break-even point and improve cash flow as part of its turnaround plan.
2027 Volvo EX60 (Source: Volvo)
As part of the restructuring, Volvo is cutting about 2,500 jobs globally, 2,000 of which are based in Sweden.
Volvo posted
of SEK -3.7 billion ($373 million) in the third quarter, with its operating profit margin falling to -5.6%.
“We continue to operate in a very tough environment with strong external challenges: de-globalization, hypercompetition and climate change,” Samuelsson said. He added, “In the short term, with severely challenged volumes, we need to reinforce our turnaround plan with additional decisive actions.”
Electrek’s Take
While Volvo struggles to ramp up production, other luxury brands, such as BMW, are also seeing early success with their next-generation electric vehicles.
The iX3, based on BMW’s Neue Klasse platform, received
over 100,000 orders
after it went on sale in October 2025.
BMW recently added a third shift at its new manufacturing plant in Debrecen, Hungary, just months after it introduced a second shift as it ramps up output.
Volvo is betting on its new SPA3 platform to lower production costs, boost profit margins, and accelerate its push into software-defined vehicles.
As part of its turnaround plan, Volvo is working on its largest-ever product push. The plans include 13 new cars through the end of 2030.

title: Tesla cancels Cybertruck in Australia and NZ after 7 years of deposits
content:
Tesla Cybertruck
Fred Lambert
| Oct 23 2026 - 7:35 am PT
Cyberbeast / Source: Tesla.com
Tesla has officially cancelled the Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand. Reservation holders are getting emails today telling them their orders are void and their deposits will be refunded.
Australians started putting down A$150 to reserve the electric pickup in November 2019. That’s almost seven years of waiting for a truck Tesla now says it won’t build for them.
“Plans… have been discontinued”
The email, which reservation holders started sharing on social media and Reddit this morning, is short.
“After careful consideration, plans to produce Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand have been discontinued,” Tesla wrote. “As a result, we’re unable to fulfil your reservation and it will be cancelled.”
Tesla says customers will get a full refund for any payments made, with refunds processed within 30 days. As a consolation, the automaker is offering a free one-year subscription to FSD (Supervised) to reservation holders who order a new Model 3 or Model Y instead.
Tesla is trying to convert a dead Cybertruck reservation into a sale of a car it actually builds in right-hand drive.
The emails went out a day after Tesla reported its Q3 2026 earnings.
Seven years of “next year”
Australia wasn’t a small market on paper. A crowdsourced survey of reservations from 2020 put it third behind the US and Canada, with about 3% of all Cybertruck reservations. Tesla never confirmed regional numbers, but by 2023, crowdsourced tracking
put total Cybertruck reservations at around 2 million
Tesla quietly closed the Australian reservation page in May 2022 and replaced it with a “Get updates” button. It didn’t refund anyone at the time. People who had already reserved just kept waiting.
Then in 2024, Tesla shipped a Cybertruck down under for a display tour, and Elon Musk told shareholders that year: “We might be able to certify it for other markets sometime next year.” Next year came and went, and the truck never got a right-hand-drive version.
That’s the core problem. The Cybertruck is built only in left-hand drive. Australia, New Zealand, the UK, and Japan all need right-hand drive, and Australia also requires certification under its own design rules. That’s a big bill for a truck with a truck that is already having demand issues in North America.
The Cybertruck can’t justify the investment
Tesla’s few international Cybertruck launches all share one thing: they’re left-hand-drive markets. Deliveries
started in South Korea late last year and in the UAE in January
, followed by configurators in Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, and Israel. The truck remains blocked in the EU, mainly for pedestrian safety reasons.
And the volumes don’t support a right-hand-drive program. Tesla delivered just 8,295 “Other Models” in Q3 2026, a category that’s now almost entirely Cybertruck since Model S and Model X production ended.
We estimate Cybertruck sales at 7,000 to 8,000 units last quarter
, roughly a 30,000-per-year pace for a production line Tesla built for 250,000 units annually.
At that rate, no CFO would sign off on re-engineering the truck for two markets that together have about 33 million people.
Electrek’s Take
This was the obvious outcome for a while, and Tesla should have said so years ago.
Taking deposits in 2019 for a truck that was supposed to start at $39,900 was one thing. Closing the order page in 2022 and letting thousands of people sit on refundable deposits for four more years without a word, while the CEO kept dangling “next year,” is another.
To be fair, a lot of Australian reservation holders likely already canceled their pre-orders. The Cybertruck that showed up in 2023 isn’t the one they reserved. It’s more expensive, has less range than promised, and its US sales have collapsed from about 39,000 in 2024 to a fraction of that today. Paying a premium for an import-ready version would have made it even worse value down under.
But it also confirms what we’ve been saying: the Cybertruck is now a niche, mostly American product. Tesla isn’t likely to invest more in it, and the international expansion is just about finding buyers for the existing left-hand-drive trucks.

title: Tesla's $10B solar factory could get 35 years of tax breaks in Texas
content:
Green Energy
tesla solar
Fred Lambert
| Oct 23 2026 - 7:25 am PT
Tesla’s proposed $10 billion “Project Crystal Sun” solar factory in Texas could get up to 35 years of local tax breaks on its equipment, according to the four agreements Fort Bend County commissioners approved on Thursday.
The vote was 4-0. And Tesla still hasn’t committed to building the plant in Texas.
first reported in August
, Tesla applied for a 10-year school property tax limitation under the state’s JETI program, through Lamar CISD and the Texas Comptroller. The plan is a vertically integrated solar plant near Richmond, southwest of Houston, that would make everything from silicon ingots to finished modules, with commercial production targeted for Q1 2029.
Lamar CISD approved the school tax piece in September. The county was next.
On October 22, the commissioners court approved items 25A to 25D on its agenda: a
Chapter 312 tax abatement
Chapter 381 incentive agreement
foreign trade zone agreement
with a payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT), and a
“true up” PILOT agreement
. Interim County Judge Daniel Wong abstained because his engineering firm has worked with Tesla.
Each agreement covers a different slice of Tesla’s tax bill, and together they run for decades.
Years 1 to 10: no county tax on equipment or inventory
The Chapter 312 agreement abates 100% of county property taxes on Tesla’s equipment and other tangible personal property at the plant for 10 tax years. The clock starts in tax year 2029 by default, but Tesla can move it to the first year after production starts, as late as 2031 without needing the county’s approval.
JETI application
splits the $10.1 billion into $1.52 billion of real property and $8.6 billion of personal property, mostly production equipment.
Land and buildings aren’t part of the deal. Anything that isn’t eligible for the abatement, including the land and buildings, stays “fully taxable at all times,” according to the agreement.
Inventory goes through the foreign trade zone deal instead. Tesla’s site would be part of Port Freeport’s Foreign-Trade Zone No. 149, which exempts eligible inventory from local property tax. In exchange for the county not objecting, Tesla agreed to make PILOT payments, set at “zero dollars or 0%” of the forgone taxes for as long as the abatement is in effect.
Years 11 to 30: Tesla gets 90% back
When the abatement ends, the Chapter 381 agreement takes over. Tesla starts paying county taxes on its equipment, and the county pays 90% of them back as an annual grant for 20 years. The county keeps 10% for its general fund.
Inventory follows the same pattern. After the abatement, Tesla’s FTZ payment rises to 10% of the taxes that would otherwise apply.
The 12,000-job bonus
There’s one more lever. If Tesla averages at least 12,000 employees for any two consecutive years during the first decade, the first five years of the rebate period become a 100% grant, and the rebate period stretches from 20 to 25 years.
That pushes the agreement out to Project Year 35. It’s also 2,288 jobs above the 9,712 Tesla says it will create.
What Tesla has to deliver
To keep the tax breaks, Tesla has to start construction by June 30, 2027, begin “regular commercial production of solar cells” by December 31, 2030, and invest $10 billion by the later of December 31, 2031 or two years after production starts. Force majeure and “ERCOT Delay” provisions can extend those dates.
The jobs ramp is 2,500, 5,000, 7,500, then 9,712 employees by the fourth year of operations, with an average compensation of $55 per hour. Tesla gets the full abatement as long as it hits 90% of the headcount target, which is about 8,741 people.
The penalties are mild. Missing a jobs or wage target for one year only costs Tesla that year’s break, and two misses in a row lets the county terminate the agreement. Full recapture of abated taxes, plus a possible 15% penalty if they aren’t repaid within 60 days, is reserved for “Material Defaults” like missing the $10 billion investment, blowing the construction deadlines or abandoning the plant for 12 months.
Under the Chapter 381 deal, grants from earlier years can’t be clawed back for a headcount shortfall.
The county’s floor is small. The true-up agreement only guarantees that Fort Bend collects at least $2 million a year, and 25% of the taxes Tesla pays on its real property, the county’s 10% share and the FTZ payments all count toward that total.
For scale, Tesla’s own consultant, Kroll, estimated in the JETI filing that the project would pay $276.5 million in Fort Bend County general taxes over 38 years without incentives, peaking at $16.2 million in 2030. That estimate lumps land, buildings and equipment together. The equipment portion is the one the county just agreed to give back, for most of those years.
Shopping for the best deal
In its application, it says the economics of the Fort Bend site are “not competitive” with an unnamed site in another state without the JETI limitation and local abatements. The competing state is redacted in a confidential supplement.
None of the documents state a production capacity. The only big number is a quote from Elon Musk at Davos in January, cited in the application: “The SpaceX and Tesla team, both separately, are working to build to 100 GW a year of solar power in the U.S., of manufactured solar power.”
For comparison, Qcells is spending $2.5 billion on its ingot-to-module campus in Cartersville, Georgia, where a 3.5 GW cell line started production this year. Crystal Sun’s budget is four times that.
Tesla has been here before. New York spent $950 million on the Buffalo factory for Tesla’s solar business, and when the solar plans fell apart, Tesla
turned to things other than solar to meet its employment requirements
, including data labeling for Autopilot. Tesla did
announce production of a new solar panel in Buffalo last year
Electrek’s Take
We want this factory to happen. A US plant making its own ingots, wafers, cells and modules would be rare, and it’s one of the few parts of Tesla’s business that still lines up with the mission it used to talk about before its “awesome abundance” pivot based on AI.
But corporate America loves its tax breaks. For 10 years, Tesla pays no county tax on the $8.6 billion of equipment that makes up most of the project. For the next 20, it gets 90% of it back. In return, the county’s guaranteed minimum is $2 million a year, on a $10 billion plant. And Tesla still hasn’t said it’s coming.
That’s how site selection works now. Companies file, collect offers from several states, and the county that bids the most wins. Fort Bend’s economic development director, Carlos Guzman, told ABC13 the county “would’ve been eliminated from consideration” without these agreements. Hard to argue with that, and it’s exactly why these deals keep getting richer.
The protections are thin too. One bad year costs Tesla a year of breaks, and past rebates can’t be clawed back over a headcount shortfall, even though the county’s goal is obviously long-term employment.
Then there’s the equipment.
Reuters reported in March
that Tesla was in talks to buy $2.9 billion of Chinese solar equipment, and its supply chain is already
caught in a patent fight between Chinese suppliers
The state still has to sign off on the school-tax piece. After that, it’s on Tesla. Is it actually building in Texas, or is Fort Bend’s offer just leverage against the other state? From what I’m hearing, Tesla is set on the Houston-area location.
Tesla wants to start making solar panels in Texas by 2029, but you don’t have to wait that long to go solar at home. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. title: Yozma IN 11 review: The OG mini e-moto gets updates galore
content:
Seth Weintraub
| Oct 23 2026 - 5:39 am PT
…including 4.5kW motor, bigger 1.4kWh battery and 45mph top speed
Yozma may not have invented the mini moto space, but they certainly helped mainstream it. Together with Tuttios and Sur Rons,
Yozma’s IN10
was one of the most popular mini motos out there, and if you surveyed the average group of 14-15-year-olds in a suburban rideout, you’d be hard-pressed not to find at least a few Yozma IN10s among them…
Today Yozma is shipping the IN 11
, which attempts to bridge the gap between entry-level mini-bikes and high-end off-roaders, but at what cost?
Taken in a vacuum, the Yozma IN11 is an impressive update to the IN 10 and actually is more closely specced to the bigger
IN10 Pro
Yozma IN 11 spec sheet:
Peak motor output, up sharply from the prior IN 10’s 2,600W baseline.
Claimed peak torque, delivering aggressive low-end climb performance.
Advertised top speed in Race mode. Real world only slightly lower
52V 27Ah = 1404Wh:
Removable lithium battery pack, promising up to 55 miles of range in Eco mode with a 5- to 6-hour recharge time. No one has time to drive for 55 miles in Eco Mode. Expect 20-30 miles when gunning it.
~$1,299:
Pre-order and promotional launch pricing. Yozma has the swag to demand a higher price point than the sub-$1,000 off-brand offerings, but it isn’t a slam-dunk decision.
Auto Wheelie Assist:
Embedded in “Stunt Mode,” this feature allows riders to cap front-wheel elevation between 15° and 40° with anti-tip protection, functioning like digital training wheels for lofting the bike. Wheelies also increase the likelihood of injuries obviously
One-button reverse gear
– helps riders maneuver tight trails and tight garage spaces without manhandling the frame.
Brake Light /
Magnetic kill switch
– nice safety features and substitute for key in some cases.
Tiered riding modes:
Four maps (Eco, Sport, Race, Stunt) let users toggle between commuter battery conservation and full-torque delivery.
But we of course, don’t live in a vacuum, and others, including the
Heybike Villain
Engwe Eagle
have already brought 52V, 4.5kW motors to the pit bike form factor, sometimes at much lower cost.
I should say here that parents who want to keep their kids’ e-motos in the 20-30mph range are going to be a whole lot happier with the 2.6kW than 4.5kW motors. Two nice safety improvements over the original Yozma IN10 include the magnetic kill switch and brake lights on the IN11.
Electrek’s take: Yozma’s advantages
If we are keeping it real here, there are dozens of similar-sized and spec’d mini-e-motos out there, often at a
much lower cost
than the Yozma IN11. But I’d argue that as the biggest and most trusted of these brands, Yozma is a safer bet.
Also, the IN11 is just a lot more solid than the random Amazon/Alibaba electric pit bike. Putting the IN11 together is quicker and easier than any other emoto I’ve built, and it just feels a lot more solid.
That feeling extends to the safety features. The brakes are more dialed in. The turning feels a lot tighter, and the overall ride is quieter and lighter. I believe, and my limited testing bears this out, that spec for spec, I got a lot more range on the IN11 than I got on other bikes with similar battery and motor specs. That 200nm of torque feels like it belongs on a much more expensive e-moto.
The wheelie mode is a nice trick (15, 25, or 40 degrees wheelie settings) and something
we’ve only seen on Anylands
for this price point so far. It is more developed on the IN11 but expect to see this on just about every new pit bike coming out over the next few years.
That said, the price, which is currently fluctuating between $1299 and $1499 (don’t forget your $60 off
Electrek
code), Yozma is going to be on the more expensive side of the 4.5kW emotos out there and some of the
newcomers are bringing an intense value competition
to the place where Yozma once dominated by itself.

title: Overhead wired charging comes to Austin electric bus fleet
content:
Electric Buses
Jo Borrás
| Oct 23 2026 - 4:05 am PT
CapMetro’s Austin transit fleets electrified two public bus lines and opened two new park-and-ride facilities featuring overhead pantograph-style wired charging equipment to help Austinites breathe a little bit easier.
Originally announced in June, CapMetro’s two new park-and-ride stations are now open. Dubbed the Goodnight Ranch and Expo Center facilities debuted alongside the agency’s Rapid 800 and 837 electric bus routes, adding upgraded passenger amenities and end-of-line charging infrastructure to support its growing fleet of electric transit buses.
At CapMetro’s main bus depot,
infrastructure partner Camber Charging supplied and installed two 1,440 kW charging systems connected to 48 industrial dispensers
. The installation provides 2.9 MW of total charging capacity,
and is designed to support overnight charging for up to 48 electric buses simultaneously
The new Goodnight Ranch and Expo Center terminals extend that infrastructure along the Rapid 800 and 837 routes with the overhead pantograph chargers that are the big news here, allowing buses to top off their batteries at the end of each line and eliminate any lingering range anxiety for the trip back.
“Instead of a typical bus holding 8 hours of charging, on-route charging takes that out to 20 to 22 hours,” explains CapMetro Chief Operations Officer and Executive VP, Andy Skabowski. “Every time that pantograph drops, we charge that bus. That’s what makes a commitment like (every) 10- to 15-minute service possible.”
New and flying
CapMetro electric bus; via Charged EVs.
The buses themselves are built on Canadian manufacturer New Flyer’s Xcelsior battery-electric transit platform (battery specs aren’t included in the release, but New Flyer claims up to 660 kWh of available capacity). And, with up to 320 all-electric hp with all its torque available at 0 rpm,
the city’s 48 electric buses will have no problem navigating Austin’s stop-and-go traffic
Camber Charging provides preventive maintenance, charger and energy management software and remote diagnostics across all three locations.

title: Austria allocates 173 MW at average price of €0.0642/kWh in PV tender - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Austria’s third solar market premium auction of 2026 attracted 195 successful bids, with a volume-weighted average price of €0.0642/kWh, slightly higher than in the previous round.
Ralph Diermann
23 Oct 2026
Markets & Policy
Highlights
Utility-scale
A solar park in Austria
Austria’s Renewable Energy Expansion Act (EAG) funding agency has published the results of the country’s third auction for solar PV market premiums in 2026. Successful bids ranged from €0.054/kWh to €0.0725/kWh, with a volume-weighted average of €0.0642/kWh, slightly higher than in the second auction round.
The auction offered 172.6 MW of solar capacity, but ultimately awarded 173.4 MW across 195 successful bids. The EAG funding agency did not disclose the level of oversubscription.
The bidding round closed on Sept. 24, 2026. Unsuccessful applicants can submit new bids in future auctions, although no further dates have been announced.
Austria’s solar market premium auctions are open to new ground-mounted and rooftop PV installations, as well as extensions of existing systems, with capacities exceeding 10 kW. Projects must not have been commissioned at the time of bidding. Ground-mounted installations on agricultural land or grassland are subject to a reduction of up to 25% in their applicable bid value, a measure designed to favor rooftop PV projects.
Austria’s second solar market premium auction, which closed on June 11, 2026, offered 179 MW of capacity. The EAG funding agency awarded contracts on July 10, with successful bids reaching a maximum of €0.0669/kWh. The ceiling was lower than the highest successful bid of €0.0725/kWh recorded in the third round, indicating an increase in the upper end of accepted bid prices.
The first auction of 2026 closed on March 17, with authorities awarding 170.97 MW against an offered volume of 175 MW. Successful bids ranged from €0.0400/kWh to €0.0680/kWh, with a volume-weighted average of €0.0634/kWh, slightly below the €0.0642/kWh recorded in the third auction.
The government had initially allocated 175 MW to each of the year’s four planned solar market premium auctions, although the capacity available in individual rounds can change. Under Austria’s auction framework, projects compete on their requested support levels, with bids ranked from lowest to highest until the available capacity is allocated.

title: Italy awards full 30 MW quota in second floating PV tender - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Italy’s second FER2 auction for floating solar projects on inland waters has allocated its entire 30 MW quota, following weak participation in the first round. Eight projects secured capacity, while two were excluded despite offering a 2% discount on the reference tariff.
Massimiliano Tripodo
23 Oct 2026
Markets & Policy
Highlights
Utility-scale
Enel’s floating PV testing facility in Catania, Italy
Italy’s second competitive bidding round for floating photovoltaic systems on inland waters under the FER2 incentive scheme has allocated its entire 30 MW quota. According to rankings published by Italian energy agency Gestore dei Servizi Energetici (GSE), two projects were excluded despite offering a 2% discount on the reference tariff.
The result marks a turnaround from the
first FER2 floating solar tender
, which allocated capacity to just one 991 kW project out of a 50 MW quota. The Italian authorities subsequently
reduced the quota to 30 MW for the second round
Of the eight successful projects, seven have capacities exceeding 1 MW and offered discounts ranging from 2.010% to 3.25% on the reference tariff.
The largest project is a 5.5 MW floating PV installation proposed by Sunprime Agira in Landiona, in the province of Novara, Piedmont. The project secured capacity with a 2.010% discount on the reference tariff of €70.6 ($82.0)/MWh.
The smallest successful project is a 380 kW installation proposed by Gens Srl in Bologna, Emilia-Romagna. It secured capacity with a 2% discount on the reference tariff of €84.7/MWh.
Rosa Rinnovabili secured allocations for five projects in Lombardy, located in the municipalities of Pioltello and Mediglia, in the province of Milan.
For the second round, reference tariffs for floating PV systems on inland waters were set at €87.3/MWh for installations between 1 kW and 300 kW, €84.7/MWh for systems between 300 kW and 1 MW, and €70.6/MWh for installations exceeding 1 MW.
In the previous round, reference tariffs stood at €90/MWh for installations between 1 kW and 1 MW and €75/MWh for systems exceeding 1 MW.
In an official notice, GSE said developers of successful projects must submit their incentive applications through the FER-E portal within 30 calendar days of the plants entering operation. The agency will notify unsuccessful applicants of the reasons for their exclusion.

title: The Hydrogen Stream: Italian company unveils seven-layer PEM electrolyzer assembly to reduce iridium use - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Another 100 companies wrote the European executive body to preserve EU green hydrogen targets. Meanwhile, the European Commission selected 77 net-zero projects, including several hydrogen projects.
Sergio Matalucci
23 Oct 2026
Markets & Policy
Energy Storage
Hydrogen
UFI Hydrogen’s new generation of proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzer membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs)-
UFI Hydrogen
has unveiled a new generation of proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzer membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs) at Hydrogen Technology World Expo in Hamburg, Germany. The Italian company, part of the UFI Group, said the platform integrates seven functional components into a single assembly, compared with three in its existing MEA technology, to reduce iridium consumption and simplify stack manufacturing. While conventional three-component MEAs require electrolyzer manufacturers to source, integrate and qualify additional components separately, the new architecture is designed to reduce supplier interfaces and streamline procurement, testing and qualification. The company said the reduction in iridium use is achieved through improvements in MEA architecture, functional components and catalyst configuration, although it has not disclosed specific catalyst loadings or performance figures. The platform can also be customized to manufacturers’ stack requirements, including geometries, dimensions, membrane characteristics, catalyst selection and component interfaces. “The MEA is the chip of electrochemistry: it is where a decisive share of an electrolyzer’s performance and competitiveness is determined,” said CEO Marco Lazzaroni. The company aims to work directly with electrolyzer manufacturers on the design and qualification of customized assemblies, reducing integration risks. The new product is undergoing industrial scale-up, with testing, validation and integration activities planned with stack manufacturers. Series production is scheduled to begin in 2027, while UFI Hydrogen’s existing three-component MEA technology will remain in production.
said it has deployed hydrogen power units (HPUs) at concerts, festivals and golf tournaments to supply electricity while reducing air pollution near stages, production areas and crowds. The UK-based company said the deployments helped protect the health of artists, crews and attendees. Its energy-as-a-service offering combines power generation equipment, hydrogen supply, transport, on-site storage and operational support. GeoPura was recently acquired by
Ballard Power Systems
Hydrogen Council
said another 100 companies have signed an industry letter urging the European Commission to maintain the Renewable Energy Directive (RED III) targets and mandates for renewable fuels of non-biological origin (RFNBOs) in transport and industry beyond 2030, bringing the total number of signatories to 260. “The letter stresses removing RFNBO targets would not simplify anything. It would waste six years of work, shake the market, punish first movers, and undermine confidence in EU climate and energy policy,” said the council, which coordinated the initiative with Hydrogen Europe and the Renewable Hydrogen Coalition. Signatories include European companies Axpo, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP), Iberdrola, De Nora, Ingeteam, Siemens Energy and Snam, as well as non-European companies Adani, Acwa Power, Air Products, Hitachi, Masdar and Toyota.
European Commission
has selected 77 net-zero technology projects across Europe for €3.4 billion ($3.9 billion) in funding from revenues generated by the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS). The selected projects include a medium-scale project in the Netherlands, small-scale projects in France and Latvia, and two pilot projects in Germany. The commission also selected a Belgian project to scale up solid oxide electrolysis cell (SOEC) technology and an Italian project to expand solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) and SOEC manufacturing. Several large-scale projects, primarily involving refineries, will focus on increasing low-carbon hydrogen production and consumption.
Oxford Institute for Energy Studies
said automated data collection through smart meters and Internet of Things (IoT) devices, robust validation and audit trails, secure digital identities, and interoperable certificate registries could facilitate compliance with hourly electricity matching requirements and hydrogen certification schemes. In a research paper examining digital measurement, reporting and verification (dMRV), the institute proposed a modular architecture covering data collection, quality assurance, eligibility and emissions calculations, evidence management, independent verification and certificate issuance. It also outlined several possible dMRV architectures, including hybrid systems, permissioned distributed ledgers and upgraded centralized registries.
Stiesdal Hydrogen
has brought a 6.5 MW electrolyzer into commercial operation at
European Energy’s
green hydrogen facility in Måde, Denmark. The system was upgraded from 3.1 MW in September 2026 and has supplied hydrogen to offtakers at operating loads of up to 6.5 MW since Sept. 29. The facility has been producing hydrogen since 2023. “The upgraded 6.5 MW system sits within the same plant. From the outside, the only visible addition is an extra converter cabinet. At nominal load, the facility can now produce up to 1,270 Nm³ of hydrogen per hour,” said the two Danish companies.
American Electric Power (AEP)
plans to invest approximately $4 billion in a 702 MW fuel cell power generation project in Wyoming, United States, under a 20-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with Google. The Ohio-based utility said construction is expected to begin in 2026, with the facility scheduled to become fully operational by the end of 2028. The project will use advanced fuel cell technology developed by
Bloom Energy
, a Dutch manufacturer of hydrogen refueling equipment, has declared bankruptcy and invited potential investors to participate in a sales process. The company said it had made progress toward a possible restart during a suspension of payments, including reaching agreements with customers, continuing projects and holding advanced discussions with prospective investors. “Although it was not possible to finalise all necessary agreements within the available timeframe, the progress achieved provides a valuable foundation for the next phase,” Resato said.

title: Chinese PV Industry Brief: Polysilicon inventories remain high - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
TrendForce said China’s polysilicon inventories remained above 560,000 metric tons despite expected production cuts in October. Persistent oversupply and weak downstream demand continued to weigh on prices.
Vincent Shaw
23 Oct 2026
Markets & Policy
TrendForce
’s EnergyTrend said on Oct. 22 that polysilicon inventories in China remained above 560,000 metric tons, despite an expected month-on-month decline of approximately 20,000 metric tons in domestic production in October. Supply continued to slightly exceed demand from downstream ingot manufacturers. EnergyTrend said polysilicon producers had discussed maintaining selling prices at or above CNY 43 ($6.32)/kg, although the proposed price floor does not necessarily reflect actual transaction prices. Elevated inventories and weak downstream demand continued to weigh on prospects for a sustained price recovery.
, a Chinese renewable energy data provider, said centralized solar module procurement tenders totaled approximately 6.6 GW between Oct. 3 and Oct. 16, up from 410 MW in the preceding two-week period. The increase was largely driven by major procurement programs from state-owned enterprises. Meanwhile, projects with announced contract awards or shortlisted bidders totaled 2.81 GW, down 35.4% from 4.35 GW in the previous period. The figures, released on Oct. 19, point to a recovery in tendering activity following China’s National Day holiday, while contract awards remained relatively subdued.
China’s Vice
Minister of Ecology and Environment Li Gao
said on Oct. 21 that China plans to raise concerns about unilateralism and trade protectionism at the COP31 climate summit in November. Li called for the free flow of green and low-carbon products and technologies, warning that trade barriers could undermine global climate action. Chinese solar modules and other clean energy products have faced increasing trade restrictions in the United States and Europe in recent years, putting the relationship between climate policy and trade measures in focus ahead of the summit.
National Energy Administration
(NEA) issued implementation guidelines on Oct. 21 to promote the integration of coal-fired power generation with renewable energy. The guidelines outline five integration models, including coordinated power transmission from renewable energy projects and coal-fired power plants, cleaner heating through combined heat and power facilities, and the integration of renewables with captive coal-fired generation. The measures encourage coal plant flexibility upgrades, transmission capacity expansion, and coordinated operations with wind and solar projects to improve renewable energy integration. Eligible projects may qualify for financial support under existing government programs. The policy aims to facilitate additional renewable energy deployment while reducing emissions from coal-fired generation.

Announced on Oct. 19, the agreement covers modules from Longi’s Hi-MO 9 series for projects in Europe and other international markets. It follows the companies’ cooperation on the 1.5 GW Khazna solar project in the United Arab Emirates. The companies did not disclose the contract value or project-specific allocations. The framework volumes do not necessarily represent firm purchase orders.

title: South Korea’s renewable energy capacity overtakes coal for first time - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Renewable energy capacity in South Korea reached 41 GW on Oct. 21, edging past coal-fired capacity for the first time, according to the country’s power market operator.
Brian Publicover
23 Oct 2026
Markets & Policy
Commercial & industrial
Utility-scale
Seoul, South Korea
South Korea’s installed renewable-energy capacity has surpassed coal-fired capacity for the first time, reaching 41,040 MW on Oct. 21, according to the Korea Power Exchange. That is 283 MW more than the country’s 40,757 MW of coal-fired capacity.
Renewables now account for 25.4% of South Korea’s installed generation capacity, making them the country’s second-largest source of installed capacity after liquefied natural gas (LNG), at 46,788 MW. The gap between renewables and LNG has narrowed to about 5,748 MW, said KPX.
Renewable capacity grew by an average of about 3,504 MW a year between the end of 2020 and the end of 2025, about 4.3 times the roughly 807 MW added annually for LNG. KPX said that if both trends continue, renewables could overtake LNG within two to three years to become South Korea’s largest source of installed generation capacity. The Export-Import Bank of Korea said it expects
South Korea to install 3.5 GW of solar
in 2026.
The figures refer to installed capacity rather than electricity generation.
KPX said it will support the government’s target of
100 GW of renewables by 2030
Grid expansion
The milestone follows a
government plan to expand grid capacity for renewables
. It aims to raise national transmission-level hosting capacity for renewables from 119 GW to 171 GW by 2030 and distribution-level capacity from 84 GW to 110 GW.
The plan also allows solar projects to connect above normal grid limits, with output curtailed when the network is constrained, and raises the solar connection limit on a distribution line from 14 MW to 16 MW and at a substation from 50 MW to 60 MW. Under the plan, grid connection rights will be linked to a reformed renewable portfolio standard (RPS) from January 2027, with access granted to projects selected through competitive bidding rather than on a first-come, first-served basis.
opened a tender
on Sept. 22 for 1,100 MW/6,600 MWh of six-hour energy storage on the mainland, plus 80 MW on Jeju Island, under 15-year contracts, with winners due to be announced in November and commissioning required by February 2029.
South Korea’s solar additions
surpassed 3.1 GW in 2024
and reached 3.1 GW again in 2025. The country’s First Renewable Energy Basic Plan, published earlier this year, includes roughly 56.2 GW of new solar capacity as part of its 100 GW renewables target.

title: Sodium-ion storage maker Peak Energy raises $108 million in GM-led round - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
A US sodium-ion battery storage company has closed a $108 million Series B round led by General Motors’ venture arm, as it prepares to start production at a 4 GWh factory in California and launch its systems in the data center market.
Brian Publicover
23 Oct 2026
Markets & Policy
Batteries
Energy Storage
Peak Energy said its oversubscribed Series B was led by GM Ventures, with participation from Maverick Silicon, Infinite Capital, Eclipse, Xora Innovation and LG Technology Ventures. The company did not disclose its valuation or the size of GM Ventures’ contribution.
Peak Energy said the funding will help it scale domestic manufacturing, fulfill more than $1 billion in existing customer orders and launch its passively cooled sodium-ion systems in the data center market. The round follows a
$55 million Series A in 2024
“The investment we announce today will supercharge Peak’s ability to scale and deliver as the world increasingly turns to passively cooled sodium-ion storage to solve our energy needs,” said Landon Mossburg, Peak’s co-founder and chief executive officer.
Order book
Peak Energy has not broken down the $1 billion figure. Its largest disclosed deal is a
multi-year phased agreement with Jupiter Power
for up to 4.75 GWh between 2027 and 2030, starting with about 720 MWh in 2027 and including an option for a further 4 GWh from 2028 to 2030.
In February, Energy Vault signed what it described as a
definitive supply agreement for 1.5 GWh
of Peak Energy systems, alongside a joint development agreement for storage serving AI data centers. Neither company has named an end customer or site. Peak Energy has also agreed to
pilot a sodium-ion system with RWE’s US business
in the Midcontinent Independent System Operator (MISO) market, though no capacity was disclosed.
When Peak
announced its factory in July
, it said it had more than 6 GWh of customer commitments.
Cell supply
Peak Energy said its 183,000-square-foot Sacramento plant is designed for up to 4 GWh of annual output, with production scheduled to begin in the first quarter of 2027. The company has put the capital investment at about $71 million.
The company currently sources cells from manufacturers in China, built to its specifications, and assembles them into containers at its facility in Burlingame, California. In June, it
partnered with GM
to co-develop next-generation sodium-ion cells with the carmaker’s Michigan battery labs.
“GM Ventures is investing to help Peak Energy continue to scale this innovative technology because we believe it has significant potential in the energy storage market as a safe, cost-effective solution using abundant, domestically sourced materials,” said Kevin McCabe, president of GM Ventures.
Peak Energy said its system, which eliminates active cooling, can cut the cost of energy by up to 20% compared with conventional storage and requires zero planned maintenance. The claims have not been independently verified.
The company
unveiled its first grid-scale system
in July 2025 at the Solar Technology Acceleration Center (SolarTAC) test facility in Colorado, and
began operating
the 3.5 MWh installation that September with nine utilities and independent power producers. It had earlier set up a
sodium-ion cell engineering center
in Colorado.

title: Transaera tests its heat pump with metal-organic framework dehumidification in apartment building - pv magazine Global
content:
Applications & Installations
U.S. startup Transaera will test its all-electric rooftop heat pump system in a multifamily residential building in Washington, D.C., with support from a $125,000 grant. The technology uses metal–organic frameworks for dehumidification and reportedly cuts energy consumption by around 40% compared with conventional rooftop HVAC units.
Emiliano Bellini
23 Oct 2026
Applications & Installations
Commercial & industrial
Heat pumps
Residential
Transaera installation on a multifamily building in Washington D.C.
U.S. startup
Transaera
announced it will test rooftop heat pump technology in a multifamily residential building in Washington D.C., United States.
The project is backed by a $125,000 grant from the National Deployment Grant Fund of The Clean Fight, a New York-based nonprofit that supports the early deployment of proven clean energy technologies.
“Building owners deciding how to electrify need operating cost reduction and want to see performance data from a building like theirs before they commit,” said Sorin Grama, CEO and co-founder of Transaera. “This project lets us prove, with independent data, that a more efficient system works as well to properly condition a whole apartment building as it does in an Amazon warehouse. Working with the largest apartment owner in the country means those results will go directly to the people making these decisions.”
The company describes its technology as a dedicated outdoor air system (DOAS), a type of heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) system that conditions incoming outdoor air for ventilation separately from a building’s primary heating and cooling equipment.
The all-electric system combines cooling, heating and dehumidification in a single platform. Operating as a heat pump, it eliminates the need for gas-fired reheating while managing both sensible and latent cooling loads in commercial buildings.
According to Transaera, a key feature of the technology is its approach to humidity control. Unlike conventional HVAC systems, which typically cool air below its dew point to remove moisture through condensation before reheating it, the DOAS uses solid desiccant materials based on metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) to extract moisture from incoming air before cooling. By separating dehumidification from the cooling process, the system is designed to reduce energy consumption and improve overall efficiency.
The company claims the technology can reduce energy use by approximately 40% compared with conventional packaged direct expansion (DX) rooftop units. It is also designed to maintain efficient operation in hot and humid climates, where high latent cooling loads make humidity management particularly challenging.
Transaera has designed the system as a drop-in replacement for conventional rooftop HVAC units. According to the manufacturer, its dimensions and weight are comparable to those of existing equipment, allowing installation within standard rooftop footprints without major structural modifications. The system can also be maintained using standard HVAC servicing procedures, eliminating the need for specialized technician training.
The technology is primarily aimed at large commercial buildings, including warehouses and logistics facilities, where managing humidity and high latent cooling loads can be particularly demanding.
announced it was conducted a
six-month field trial
of the rooftop heat pump at one of its logistics facilities in the United States.
“At Amazon, we seek technologies that support our Climate Pledge goal to reach net zero carbon emissions by 2040. Our work with Transaera has moved from field trial to readiness for first commercial use, and this new collaboration supports expanding use of this technology within our global network of buildings,” said at the time Asad Jafry, Director of Global Energy, Sustainability and AGV at Amazon.

title: European solar, BESS marketplace expands to Romania - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Solmeria, an online marketplace for selling solar and battery energy storage systems directly to buyers, is now listing projects in Romania alongside offers in France and Italy.
Patrick Jowett
23 Oct 2026
Markets & Policy
Commercial & industrial
European renewable energy marketplace Solmeria has expanded to include solar and battery energy storage systems (BESS) in Romania.
The marketplace, which spans ground-mounted PV, agriPV, C&I solar and BESS projects at all stages of development,
initially went live in July
with 25 projects in France.
It added its first two listings in Romania earlier this month. The two offers are both agrivoltaic installations with four-hour storage systems located in Cluj county, northwestern Romania. They have a combined capacity of 6.2 MW of solar and a total BESS capacity of 6 MW/24 MWh.
Maxime Courtaigne, CEO of Solmeria, told
pv magazine
the Romania listings now also include a ready-to-build hybrid park of 55 MWp with 193 MWh of storage. “The first listings have already received around ten expressions of interest from buyers,” he added.
Created at the request of developers, the marketplace is aiming to bring liquidity to listed projects, accelerate transactions and reduce intermediation costs. Commission is only payable only upon successful completion of a sale and is significantly lower than that of a traditional merger and acquisitions agency, according to previous reports.
Courtaigne also told
pv magazine
18 of the 25 French projects listed in the marketplace are now in sale discussions. The marketplace also opened in the Italian market in September.
He added there are more than 300 registered acquirers to date, the majority of which are French and Italian, with “dozens more joining every month.”
“France showed us that selling projects one by one to the right buyer works at every size: a 1 MWp project drew 35 expressions of interest,” Courtaigne said.
“Romania is on the same path, with around ten already on our first listings and a 55 MWp hybrid park now on the platform. Sell one project to the right buyer, and the portfolio will follow.”

title: Hemispherical perovskite solar cell design reduces sensitivity to sunlight angle - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
Chinese researchers have designed a hemispherical perovskite solar cell with a textured surface to improve light absorption and reduce sensitivity to sunlight incidence angles. Simulations showed absorption exceeding 95% and an average maximum power output of 28.25 mW/cm² across incidence angles of 0° to 50°.
Lior Kahana
23 Oct 2026
Research & Development
Cells & modules
Illustration of a hemispherical perovskite solar cell with a textured outer surface
A research team in China has proposed a hemispherical perovskite solar cell with a textured surface designed to reduce sensitivity to the angle of incident sunlight. The hemispherical geometry is intended to enable radial charge collection, while the textured surface scatters incoming light in multiple directions to enhance absorption and promote more uniform charge generation.
“Perovskite solar cells have attracted intensive research interest as a promising candidate for next-generation photovoltaic technologies, offering high power conversion efficiency and low manufacturing cost,” the researchers said. “However, the practical energy yield of conventional planar perovskite cells is severely compromised by optical losses under varying solar incidence angles, leading to significant power fluctuations that undermine their viability for renewable energy generation.”
To evaluate the design, the researchers modeled five cell architectures: planar, nanowire, smooth hemispherical, and hemispherical structures with rounded-cone or textured rounded-cone front surfaces. Each device consisted of an indium tin oxide (ITO) electrode, a phenyl-C61-butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM) electron transport layer, a methylammonium lead iodide (CH₃NH₃PbI₃) perovskite absorber, a nickel oxide (NiO) hole transport layer, and a silver (Ag) rear electrode.
The researchers used Lumerical software to simulate the five architectures, analyzing light absorption, scattering, electromagnetic fields, and charge generation across wavelengths ranging from 300 nm to 800 nm and incidence angles from 0° to 50°. They then incorporated the resulting charge-generation profiles into electrical simulations that accounted for carrier transport and recombination. The simulations were used to calculate current-voltage characteristics, power conversion efficiency, and maximum power output under different illumination angles.
Across incidence angles ranging from 0° to 50°, the textured rounded-cone cell achieved an average short-circuit current density of 25.47 mA/cm², compared with 24.03 mA/cm² for the smooth hemispherical cell and 22.52 mA/cm² for the planar device. It also achieved an average maximum power output of 28.25 mW/cm² and light absorption exceeding 95%.
“The design effectively decouples device performance from incident light angle, overcoming the critical challenge of angular-dependent power output,” the researchers concluded. “The three-dimensional hemisphere symmetry enables balanced carrier transport, while the Mie resonances induced within the perovskite shell ensure efficient light trapping.”
The solar cell concept was presented in the study “
Angle-robust photovoltaics via Mie resonance hybridization for stable power output in perovskite solar cells
,” published in
Solar Energy
. The research team included scientists from China’s Jilin Normal University and the
Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Panasonic begins sales of glass-based perovskite solar panels - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
Panasonic began commercial sales of its glass-based perovskite solar panels in September 2026, ahead of the planned launch of full-scale mass production in April 2029. The initial products are manufactured at the company’s development facility in Moriguchi, Osaka Prefecture.
Vincent Shaw
23 Oct 2026
Research & Development
Commercial & industrial
Residential
The mass-produced products, scheduled for launch in April 2029, will feature larger dimensions of up to 1.8 m × 1.2 m and additional glass thickness configurations of 4 mm x 4 mm and 5mm x 5 mm.
Japanese electronics manufacturer
Panasonic Holdings
announced it will start full-scale mass production of
glass-based perovskite solar panels
for applications in building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV) one year ahead of schedule.
The company had originally planned to start production in fiscal year 2030, which in Japan runs from April 1, 2030, to March 31, 2031.
“Ahead of full-scale mass production, we began commercial activities in September 2026 by selling pre-production products manufactured at Panasonic HD’s development facility in Moriguchi, Osaka Prefecture,” the company said in a statement. “Going forward, we aim to establish mass-production technologies at our Nagahama facility and accelerate market development through the commercial deployment of these initial products.”
“Panasonic HD was selected for a Green Innovation Fund project by the New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO) in September 2025 and has since been developing mass-production and installation technologies for glass-based perovskite solar cells,” it went on to say. “Given the progress in these technologies, growing market demand, and supportive government policies, the company has decided to bring forward the start of full-scale mass production from its original schedule.”
The modules’ graphic patterns
Panasonic said its pre-production glass-based perovskite solar panels feature a laminated-glass structure, with maximum dimensions of 1.8 m × 1.0 m and glass thickness configurations of 3+3 mm or 6+6 mm. The products are available with float glass or high-strength glass and support customized decorative designs.
The mass-produced products, scheduled for launch in April 2029, will feature larger dimensions of up to 1.8 m × 1.2 m and additional glass thickness configurations of 4+4 mm and 5+5 mm. They will also be available in laminated insulating glass configurations, with tempered glass offered as an additional option.
According to the company, both product generations comply with Japanese building standards and have passed internal tests based on IEC 61730 and IEC 62790. Panasonic also said it plans to pursue module certification in line with customer requirements and market developments.
The company uses inkjet coating, laser processing and glass encapsulation technologies in the manufacturing process. It said the technology enables customized dimensions, transparency levels and decorative patterns, making the products suitable for building-integrated photovoltaic applications, including windows and facades.
Panasonic did not disclose the modules’ power conversion efficiency, rated power output, temperature coefficient, expected service life or pricing.
The Japanese electronics manufacturer has been developing perovskite solar technology for more than a decade. In 2020, the company
unveiled a lightweight perovskite solar module
with a power conversion efficiency of 16.09% and an area of 802 cm², manufactured using an inkjet coating process.
In 2023, it
began testing glass-based perovskite solar panels
in a building in Fujisawa, Kanagawa Prefecture, in cooperation with property developer Mitsui Fudosan Residential. The company subsequently achieved a certified efficiency of 18.1% for an 802 cm² device.
More recently, in December 2025, Panasonic and Japanese building materials manufacturer YKK AP
tested the technology in office windows
, focusing on installation methods and design flexibility.
The commercialization efforts come as the Japanese government seeks to establish a domestic perovskite solar industry. In November 2024, the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
announced a target
of deploying around 20 GW of perovskite solar capacity by 2040.
The government also outlined plans to support domestic manufacturing and reduce production costs to JPY 14 ($0.09)/W by 2030 and JPY 10/W by 2040. In September 2025, the Ministry of the Environment
introduced subsidy programs
to support early deployment of perovskite solar cells and their integration with battery storage systems.
Japan has since stepped up its support for the technology. In May 2026, NEDO
opened a supplementary funding call
under its Green Innovation Fund to advance mass-production technologies for single-junction perovskite solar cells.
In September, the Ministry of the Environment
announced plans
to exclude conventional silicon solar panels from newly introduced subsidy programs starting in fiscal 2027, prioritizing perovskite and other next-generation solar technologies. The policy shift is intended to strengthen Japan’s industrial competitiveness and accelerate the commercialization of emerging photovoltaic technologies.

title: Schrödinger’s toy hidden-variable model revealed in unpublished manuscript
content: An unpublished, undated manuscript belonging to Erwin Schrödinger lies in the Austrian Central Library for Physics at the University of Vienna. Physicist Flavio Del Santo at the University of Geneva retrieved it and analyzed its contents to establish a likely date it was written and also what the famous physicist thought about random outcomes in quantum physics. The draft is titled ‘Collapse of Determinism’ and addresses one of the major problems in quantum physics – randomness of events. Quantum theory is usually used to predict the probabilities of measurement but never specific outcomes. Physicists have wondered whether this is a result of incomplete knowledge of the domain. For instance, the outcome of a coin toss seems random at first. However, if one has information about how hard the coin was tossed and the speed of the wind in the area of the toss, then there is reliable information to predict the outcome too. In the quantum realm, much remains uncertain. However, if particles carry information that determines their behavior, would they become more predictable or deterministic? What famous physicists thoughtThe debate between determinism and indeterminism in quantum mechanics has split the physicists into two groups that stand strongly by their views. While Einstein, David Bohm, and Schrödinger are often seen as champions of determinism in scientific history, Santo argues that there stance was more nuanced and less polarised than many think. Schrödinger’s unpublished manuscript is a case in point. Quantum particles carrying information that could determine their behavior is termed hidden variables, since this information might not be accessible for scientists to observe it. In 1932, mathematician John von Neumann published a result that suggested that hidden variables should not be added to quantum mechanics, During World War II, Taylor Whittaker, a British physicist and mathematician, questioned determinism, invoking Neurman’s work and citing an example of polarized light passing through a polarizer. In this setup, the angle between the polarized light and the polarizer determines how much light can pass through the latter. Quantum mechanics expresses the outcome as a probability. However, Whittaker used two values for hidden variables in this hypothesis and argued that these could not reproduce the changes that were created when the polarizer was turned. Schrondinger’s manuscript is a response to this assumption. What Schrödinger wroteIn his three-page manuscript, Schrondinger questions the restriction built into Whittaker’s reasoning and wonders why hidden variables had only two possible values. Instead, he suggested an alternative where each photon was assigned a value between zero and one. The numbers were distributed evenly across the incoming beam, and whether the photon passed the polarizer depended on its number and the polarizer’s angle. Across photons, the setup reproduced the expected transmission rate, which can be predicted using Malus’ law, but each individual outcome depended on the apparatus setting and the proposed number of the photon. Schrodinger’s manuscript also solves the problem that arises after the first measurement, where the distribution changes. So, he created a mathematical rule that changes the photon’s number after it is transmitted or reflected and restores the distribution as per Malus’ law. The question then remains is why did Schrödinger not publish this? According to Del Santo, this was likely because Heinrich Pelzer, an Austrian physicist, challenged Whittaker in a published paper. Although Pelzer’s approach was different, it still made the same point. Del Santo warns that the manuscript must not be used to claim that Schrondinger sided with a deterministic view of nature. This unpublished work could be a test of an argument rather than endorse the model, Del Santo wrote in a analysis paper. This paper can be found on the preprint server arXiv.
